subject: Urgent: Throttle surge — project quota 'ghosting' causing 429s
participants_external: emily.park@healthsync.com (Emily Park, HealthSync - Head of Engineering)
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@healthsync.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T05:42:00Z
Subject: Spike in 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Hi Naomi / Monica,

We started seeing a large spike in 429s and request timeouts against the Redwood endpoint for our main ingestion project (project id: hs-main-prod) beginning ~05:20 UTC. Errors jumped from ~0.3% to ~12% in a five-minute window; our retries amplified the load and a number of downstream workers are now failing.

Attached is a small sample of the client-side logs and a traffic snapshot. We're in the middle of a processing batch and need guidance - is this a rate-limiter change on Redwood or something on our side?

Attachments: healthsync_429_sample.log (text), traffic_snapshot_20261022.csv (csv)

Please escalate if needed — this is impacting customer-facing SLAs.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Park
Head of Engineering, HealthSync
emily.park@healthsync.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T05:49:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Monica/Marcus/Rishi — FYI, HealthSync reporting a sudden 429/timeouts surge on hs-main-prod. They attached logs; sample shows tight retry loops and a lot of client-side concurrent bursts.

Initial ask: can infra check project->org quota mappings and any recent tiering/policy changes? We saw a similar pattern last quarter where an aliasing bug caused project quota to be treated as default tier (ghosting) causing unexpected hard caps.

Immediate mitigations we can consider:
- Apply an emergency per-project quota override (5-10 minutes) to stop 429s while we triage.
- Add a temporary routing rule to send HealthSync to a compatible, higher-throughput model variant.
- Disable an aggressive client-side retry policy if they agree.

Marcus — can you take point on quota mapping + quick audit? Rishi — loop in billing/TP if we need an override/credit.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
aomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T06:05:30Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

I pulled the mapping logs and overlayed the project labels. Quick summary:
- hs-main-prod appears to have been migrated yesterday as part of a bulk label sync. The project label changed from "enterprise-tier" -> "standard-tier" but the quota alias did not update (alias pointer still referenced the old org-level quota).
- Our rate limiter enforces by effective_quota pointer. In this case the project ended up with the more restrictive default for a windowed allocation; requests surged into that window and hit the hard cap causing 429s.

Action I'm taking now:
1) Pushing emergency override: bump pool for hs-main-prod to +3x for 20 minutes (apply now).
2) Enabling temporary routing to high-throughput pool in us-east to avoid cold-start of new nodes.
3) Capturing full audit logs and creating a diagnostic snapshot (link to follow).

I expect 429s to drop within 2-5 minutes of the override. If customer continues heavy retry bursts we'll need them to back off.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@healthsync.com>, ops@healthsync.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T06:12:10Z
Subject: HealthSync: emergency override applied — immediate mitigation steps

Hi Emily / HealthSync SREs,

Quick update from infra: we applied an emergency quota override to hs-main-prod at 06:09 UTC and routed traffic to an available high-throughput pool in us-east. You should see 429s drop almost immediately.

Two asks on your side to help stabilize:
- If possible, disable aggressive client retries for 10 minutes or implement exponential backoff (max backoff 2s) while we run the snapshot.
- Send any additional log slices (request ids) to ops@healthsync.com and cc marcus_lin@redwood.com so we can correlate.

We will follow up with a short postmortem and a longer-term fix plan. Apologies for the disruption.

Attachments: traffic_snapshot_20261022.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T14:03:00Z
Subject: Escalation to leadership: quota aliasing root cause + recommendation

Naomi — summary for exec: HealthSync experienced a 12% 429 spike from 05:20–05:35 UTC due to a label-sync migration that left the project tied to an incorrect quota alias (reverting it to a lower-cap default). The emergency override removed the immediate pain; error rates reduced to ~0.2% by ~06:15 UTC.

Recommended next steps for leadership approval:
- Approve temporary account credit (pro-rated) for the impacted 1.5 hours while we complete postmortem. Estimated ~$650 — request approval to bill as goodwill.
- Approve 2-week change window to roll out a quota alias safety-check in label-sync job (reject silent alias mismatches).
- Authorize an alert rule for quota mismatch rate that pings on-call + account exec immediately.

Please confirm and I will open a formal Ops-PR to implement the safety-check and schedule a follow-up with HealthSync procurement if they request contract language.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed (post-incident plan)

Emily — again, apologies for the interruption this morning. To confirm:
- Mitigation applied at 06:09 UTC (quota override + routing) — error rate returned to baseline by 06:15 UTC.
- We have captured audit logs and created ticket RI-8421 with a diagnostic snapshot (link below).

Next steps:
1) Rishi will open an Ops-PR to add a quota-alias safety-check in the label-sync pipeline (ETA 2 weeks).
2) Marcus will publish a short-runbook for emergency overrides and update the on-call checklist.
3) Naomi/Account Exec will propose a goodwill credit — Rishi please confirm the number and I'll sign off for approval.

We will schedule a 30-minute postmortem with your team (Emily) tomorrow to walk the timeline and preventive changes. Would 10:00 AM ET work for you?

Attachments: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-8421 (diagnostic ticket)

Thanks for the quick coordination and patience — we'll follow up with a formal postmortem doc.

Best,
